question: What are the main risks Apple describes about its supply chain and foreign exchange?

answer.summary: Apple's Item 1A Risk Factors identify foreign exchange and supply chain as primary exposures. FX exposure centers on non-U.S. dollar-denominated sales, cost of sales and operating expenses worldwide, with gross margins on foreign products and products using foreign-sourced components vulnerable to FX fluctuations [T00221]. The value of the U.S. dollar relative to local currencies also affects financial performance [T00220]. Supply chain risks include credit exposure on trade receivables, vendor non-trade receivables and prepayments tied to long-term supply agreements, heightened during economic downturns [T00228]. Broader business interruption risks from political events, trade disputes, war, natural disasters and public health issues could disrupt suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers and channel partners [T00123]. These risks coincided with FY2023 revenue declining 2.8% to $383.29B [F00013], where Mac was the largest contributor to the product-level decline at -$10.82B (-26.9%), 98% of the total change [F00282] [F00283], partly offset by Services growth of $7.07B (+9.1%) [F00010] [F00011].

By geography, the US was the largest contributor to the revenue decline at -$9.29B (-6.3%), 84% of the total change [F00877] [F00878], and Americas -$7.10B (-4.2%), 64% of the total change [F00838] [F00839]
